title: Apple Racing to Make Siri More Agentic Under CEO Pressure
summary: Apple CEO John Ternus is pushing AI chief Craig Federighi to accelerate Siri's agentic AI roadmap to compete with OpenAI Dots and Meta Muse by late 2026.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Apple CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI chief Craig Federighi to accelerate Siri's transformation into a competitive agentic AI assistant.
- The upgraded Siri aims to match capabilities of OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse agents, expected later in 2026.
- Despite delivering functional Siri AI on a short timeline, Apple acknowledges it still lags behind leading AI assistants.


Apple is intensifying efforts to transform Siri into a powerful[agentic AI](https://emergent.sh/glossary/what-is-agentic-ai) assistant, with CEO John Ternus applying pressure on AI chief Craig Federighi to accelerate the development roadmap. According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, the urgency stems from competitive threats posed by OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse, both of which have demonstrated advanced autonomous capabilities that current Siri iterations cannot match.


## Executive Pressure Drives Accelerated Timeline


John Ternus, who took over as Apple CEO, has made agentic AI capabilities a strategic priority for the company's voice assistant platform. Sources indicate Ternus is pushing Federighi's team to compress timelines and deliver a Siri version capable of executing complex, multi-step tasks without constant user intervention. This represents a fundamental shift from Siri's current command-and-response model to a proactive agent that can understand context, make decisions, and complete workflows autonomously.


The pressure reflects Apple's acknowledgment that it has fallen behind competitors in the AI assistant space. While Federighi's team delivered a functional Siri AI update on an accelerated schedule, internal assessments suggest the technology still lacks the sophisticated reasoning and task execution capabilities that define true agentic AI systems.


## Competing With OpenAI and Meta


The competitive landscape has shifted dramatically with OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse establishing new benchmarks for what users expect from AI assistants. These platforms can handle complex workflows spanning multiple applications, learn from user behavior patterns, and execute tasks with minimal supervision. Apple's current Siri implementation, despite recent improvements, operates primarily as a reactive interface rather than a proactive agent.


Industry observers note that Apple's traditional approach of perfecting features before release conflicts with the rapid iteration cycles driving AI development at competitors. The company must balance its quality standards with the need to ship competitive agentic capabilities before losing further ground in the AI assistant market.


## Expected Release Timeline


While Apple has not officially confirmed a launch date, the enhanced agentic Siri is expected to release on an unspecified 2026 timeline, with development sources suggesting a possible unveiling at a fall product event. The accelerated roadmap aims to integrate deep learning models that enable Siri to perform multi-step reasoning, maintain conversation context across sessions, and coordinate actions between Apple's ecosystem of devices and services.


The upgrade will reportedly include enhanced on-device processing capabilities, allowing more complex AI operations to run locally rather than requiring cloud connectivity. This aligns with Apple's longstanding privacy commitments while enabling the responsiveness that agentic AI applications demand.


## Technical Challenges and Strategic Implications


Developing true agentic AI capabilities presents significant technical hurdles for Apple's team. The system must reliably understand user intent, navigate ambiguous requests, and execute actions across third-party applications while maintaining security and privacy standards. Apple's walled-garden approach, while beneficial for user experience consistency, complicates integration with the broader app ecosystem that competing assistants leverage.


The strategic importance extends beyond consumer devices. Enterprise customers increasingly demand AI assistants capable of handling complex business workflows, and Apple's position in the corporate market depends partly on Siri's ability to compete with productivity-focused AI agents from Microsoft, Google, and other enterprise software providers.


## What This Means


Apple's accelerated push to make Siri more agentic signals recognition that AI assistants have evolved beyond simple voice commands into platforms capable of genuine task automation. The pressure from Ternus reflects both competitive necessity and the broader industry shift toward autonomous AI systems that can act as true digital assistants rather than glorified search interfaces. Whether Apple can compress its development timeline without compromising the polish users expect will determine its position in the next phase of personal AI computing.
